general.text: Always include a clear, concise executive summary (1-2 sentences) at the start of written work to highlight key issues, conclusions, and next steps for the reader.

history.text: Always include a clear, concise executive summary (1-2 sentences) at the start of written work to highlight key issues, conclusions, and next steps for the reader.

general.text: Read instructions or client requests twice before starting—first for context, second for specific tasks. Note deadlines, deliverable formats, and priority questions.

history.text: Read instructions or client requests twice before starting—first for context, second for specific tasks. Note deadlines, deliverable formats, and priority questions.

general.text: Verify all citations, dates, names, and numbers in drafts against source documents. Cross-check calculations (e.g., interest, deadlines) for accuracy.

history.text: Verify all citations, dates, names, and numbers in drafts against source documents. Cross-check calculations (e.g., interest, deadlines) for accuracy.

general.text: Use headings, bullet points, and white space to improve readability. Avoid dense paragraphs; break down complex ideas into digestible sections.

history.text: Use headings, bullet points, and white space to improve readability. Avoid dense paragraphs; break down complex ideas into digestible sections.

general.text: Run a spell-check and grammar check before finalizing work. Read aloud to catch awkward phrasing or errors automated tools might miss.

history.text: Run a spell-check and grammar check before finalizing work. Read aloud to catch awkward phrasing or errors automated tools might miss.

general.text: Save drafts with version numbers (e.g., _v1, _v2) and timestamps. Use descriptive file names (e.g., [Client]_[Matter]_[Date]_[Draft/Final]).

history.text: Save drafts with version numbers (e.g., _v1, _v2) and timestamps. Use descriptive file names (e.g., [Client]_[Matter]_[Date]_[Draft/Final]).

general.text: Confirm the document’s purpose before drafting: Is it advisory, transactional, or litigation-focused? Tailor tone, detail, and structure accordingly.

history.text: Confirm the document’s purpose before drafting: Is it advisory, transactional, or litigation-focused? Tailor tone, detail, and structure accordingly.

general.text: Ask for feedback early—share outlines or rough drafts with supervisors to align on direction. Clarify expectations before investing time in polishing.

history.text: Ask for feedback early—share outlines or rough drafts with supervisors to align on direction. Clarify expectations before investing time in polishing.

analysis.text: Always verify key details: dates, names, figures, and definitions. Cross-reference with original documents or reliable sources to ensure accuracy before finalizing.

history.text: Always verify key details: dates, names, figures, and definitions. Cross-reference with original documents or reliable sources to ensure accuracy before finalizing.

analysis.text: Break complex tasks into smaller steps. Tackle one issue at a time—summarize facts, identify legal questions, then apply law—before synthesizing into a coherent analysis.

history.text: Break complex tasks into smaller steps. Tackle one issue at a time—summarize facts, identify legal questions, then apply law—before synthesizing into a coherent analysis.

analysis.text: For legal analysis, include: (1) facts, (2) legal issue, (3) relevant law, (4) application, (5) conclusion. Omit any section only if irrelevant, but justify omissions.

history.text: For legal analysis, include: (1) facts, (2) legal issue, (3) relevant law, (4) application, (5) conclusion. Omit any section only if irrelevant, but justify omissions.

analysis.text: Read statutes, judgments, or contracts *actively*—highlight ambiguities, note gaps, and flag inconsistencies. Passive reading leads to oversight; engage with the text critically.

history.text: Read statutes, judgments, or contracts *actively*—highlight ambiguities, note gaps, and flag inconsistencies. Passive reading leads to oversight; engage with the text critically.

analysis.text: Double-check calculations (e.g., damages, deadlines). Use formulas, spreadsheets, or calculators, and document assumptions. Errors here are often costly and avoidable.

history.text: Double-check calculations (e.g., damages, deadlines). Use formulas, spreadsheets, or calculators, and document assumptions. Errors here are often costly and avoidable.

analysis.text: Develop a consistent method for legal research. Start with primary sources (legislation, cases), then secondary (commentary), and note jurisdiction-specific nuances early.

history.text: Develop a consistent method for legal research. Start with primary sources (legislation, cases), then secondary (commentary), and note jurisdiction-specific nuances early.

analysis.text: For due diligence or compliance checks, create a checklist tailored to the matter (e.g., regulatory requirements). Systematically tick off items to avoid missed steps.

history.text: For due diligence or compliance checks, create a checklist tailored to the matter (e.g., regulatory requirements). Systematically tick off items to avoid missed steps.

analysis.text: Time management: Allocate blocks for deep work (analysis) and shallow work (admin). Avoid multitasking—focus on one task at a time to reduce errors and improve clarity.

history.text: Time management: Allocate blocks for deep work (analysis) and shallow work (admin). Avoid multitasking—focus on one task at a time to reduce errors and improve clarity.

drafting.text: Always include a clear title, date, and version number on every document. Label sections logically (e.g., 'Background,' 'Analysis,' 'Recommendations') to ensure readability and ease of reference.

history.text: Always include a clear title, date, and version number on every document. Label sections logically (e.g., 'Background,' 'Analysis,' 'Recommendations') to ensure readability and ease of reference.

drafting.text: Draft in plain language first, then refine for precision. Avoid jargon unless necessary—define technical terms if used. This ensures clarity before legal rigor.

history.text: Draft in plain language first, then refine for precision. Avoid jargon unless necessary—define technical terms if used. This ensures clarity before legal rigor.

drafting.text: Verify all citations (cases, statutes, clauses) are accurate and up-to-date. Cross-check references to ensure they align with the document’s purpose and jurisdiction.

history.text: Verify all citations (cases, statutes, clauses) are accurate and up-to-date. Cross-check references to ensure they align with the document’s purpose and jurisdiction.

drafting.text: Use active voice for clarity and conciseness (e.g., 'The party must prove' vs. 'Proof is required by the party'). Passive voice can obscure responsibility.

history.text: Use active voice for clarity and conciseness (e.g., 'The party must prove' vs. 'Proof is required by the party'). Passive voice can obscure responsibility.

drafting.text: Include a summary or executive overview for long documents. Highlight key actions, deadlines, or risks upfront to aid quick understanding.

history.text: Include a summary or executive overview for long documents. Highlight key actions, deadlines, or risks upfront to aid quick understanding.

drafting.text: Break down complex ideas into bullet points or numbered lists. This improves readability and helps the reader follow logical steps or arguments.

history.text: Break down complex ideas into bullet points or numbered lists. This improves readability and helps the reader follow logical steps or arguments.

drafting.text: Proofread for consistency: defined terms, formatting (fonts, spacing), and numbering. Ensure all cross-references (e.g., 'Section 3.2') are correct.

history.text: Proofread for consistency: defined terms, formatting (fonts, spacing), and numbering. Ensure all cross-references (e.g., 'Section 3.2') are correct.

drafting.text: Draft iteratively: create a rough outline, fill in details, then refine. Review with fresh eyes or after a break to catch errors or gaps.

history.text: Draft iteratively: create a rough outline, fill in details, then refine. Review with fresh eyes or after a break to catch errors or gaps.

review.text: Before finalizing, verify every citation, definition, and cross-reference aligns with the source. Ensure no ambiguous terms, gaps, or contradictions exist in the document’s logic or legal positions.

history.text: Before finalizing, verify every citation, definition, and cross-reference aligns with the source. Ensure no ambiguous terms, gaps, or contradictions exist in the document’s logic or legal positions.

review.text: Read your draft aloud to catch awkward phrasing, missing words, or unclear transitions. This forces you to engage critically with the text, not just skim.

history.text: Read your draft aloud to catch awkward phrasing, missing words, or unclear transitions. This forces you to engage critically with the text, not just skim.

review.text: For calculations (e.g., damages, deadlines), re-run numbers manually or use a separate tool. Cross-check assumptions, formulas, and inputs against the underlying facts.

history.text: For calculations (e.g., damages, deadlines), re-run numbers manually or use a separate tool. Cross-check assumptions, formulas, and inputs against the underlying facts.

review.text: Use a two-pass review: first for substance (arguments, accuracy), second for form (grammar, formatting). Avoid trying to fix everything at once—focus narrows errors.

history.text: Use a two-pass review: first for substance (arguments, accuracy), second for form (grammar, formatting). Avoid trying to fix everything at once—focus narrows errors.

review.text: Confirm all required elements are present: headers, signatures, exhibits, confidentiality notices, or jurisdictional statements. Missing one can invalidate the document.

history.text: Confirm all required elements are present: headers, signatures, exhibits, confidentiality notices, or jurisdictional statements. Missing one can invalidate the document.

review.text: If reviewing others’ work, note recurring errors (e.g., typos, formatting). Apply these lessons to your own drafting to preempt common mistakes.

history.text: If reviewing others’ work, note recurring errors (e.g., typos, formatting). Apply these lessons to your own drafting to preempt common mistakes.

review.text: Check for internal consistency: party names, dates, and key terms must match across the document. Inconsistencies undermine credibility and create confusion.

history.text: Check for internal consistency: party names, dates, and key terms must match across the document. Inconsistencies undermine credibility and create confusion.

review.text: Schedule reviews with fresh eyes—ideally after a break. Fatigue reduces attention to detail; stepping away sharpens objectivity.

history.text: Schedule reviews with fresh eyes—ideally after a break. Fatigue reduces attention to detail; stepping away sharpens objectivity.
